\begin{proof}
Let $G$ be a group of order $9=3^2$. By the class equation,
\[
|G|=|Z(G)|+\sum_i [G:C_G(x_i)],
\]
where the sum runs over representatives of the noncentral conjugacy classes. Every index in the sum is a power of $3$ greater than $1$, hence is divisible by $3$. Therefore $|Z(G)|$ is divisible by $3$. Thus $|Z(G)|$ is either $3$ or $9$.

If $|Z(G)|=9$, then $G=Z(G)$ and $G$ is abelian. Suppose instead that $|Z(G)|=3$. Then $G/Z(G)$ has order $3$, so it is cyclic. A group whose quotient by its center is cyclic is abelian: if $G/Z(G)=\langle gZ(G)\rangle$, then every element has the form $g^iz$ with $z\in Z(G)$, and such elements commute. Hence $G$ is abelian in this case as well.

Therefore every group of order $9$ is abelian.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
Let $G$ be a group of order $9$. By the class equation, the size of every conjugacy class is either $1$ or a divisor of $9$ greater than $1$, hence every noncentral conjugacy class has size $3$ or $9$. Consequently,
\[
9=|G|=|Z(G)|+3m
\]
for some integer $m$, so $3\mid |Z(G)|$.

If $|Z(G)|=9$, then $G=Z(G)$ and $G$ is abelian. If $|Z(G)|=3$, then $G/Z(G)$ has order $3$, and therefore is cyclic. Let $G/Z(G)=\langle gZ(G)\rangle$. For any $x,y\in G$, write $x=g^iz$ and $y=g^jw$ with $z,w\in Z(G)$. Then
\[
xy=g^{i+j}zw=g^{i+j}wz=yx,
\]
so $G$ is abelian.

Thus every group of order $9$ is abelian.
\end{proof}

\begin{proof}
Let $G$ be a group of order $9$. We use the class equation. For every $x\in G$, the size of its conjugacy class is $[G:C_G(x)]$, which divides $|G|=9$. Thus each conjugacy class has size $1$, $3$, or $9$. The classes of size $1$ are precisely the elements of $Z(G)$, and all other classes have size divisible by $3$. Hence
\[
9=|Z(G)|+3m
\]
for some integer $m$, so $3$ divides $|Z(G)|$.

Therefore $|Z(G)|$ is either $3$ or $9$. If $|Z(G)|=9$, then $Z(G)=G$, so $G$ is abelian. If $|Z(G)|=3$, then $|G/Z(G)|=3$, so $G/Z(G)$ is cyclic. Choose $g\in G$ such that $G/Z(G)=\langle gZ(G)\rangle$. For any $x,y\in G$, there exist integers $r,s$ and elements $z,w\in Z(G)$ such that $x=g^rz$ and $y=g^sw$. Since $z,w$ are central,
\[
xy=g^{r+s}zw=g^{r+s}wz=yx.
\]
Thus $G$ is abelian.

Hence every group of order $9$ is abelian.
\end{proof}
